record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
record.original_question: Does there exist a nuclear F-space that is locally pseudo-convex but not locally convex?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 9* - Does a nuclear locally pseudo-convex non-locally convex F-space exist ?
After the Conference J.P. Ligaud has shown that each nuclear locally pseudo-convex space is locally convex

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall the following definitions. A topological vector space $X$ over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ is called an F-space if its topology is induced by a complete translation-invariant metric. A subset $U$ of $X$ is called $p$-convex (for some $0 < p \le 1$) if for all $x, y \in U$ and all scalars $\alpha, \beta \ge 0$ with $\alpha^p + \beta^p = 1$ one has $\alpha x + \beta y \in U$. The space $X$ is called locally pseudo-convex if it has a base of neighborhoods of $0$ each of which is $p$-convex for some $p \in (0,1]$ (the value of $p$ may depend on the neighborhood). It is locally convex if it has a base of convex (i.e. $1$-convex) neighborhoods of $0$. A locally pseudo-convex space $X$ is called nuclear if for every continuous $p$-homogeneous seminorm $q$ on $X$ there exists a continuous $r$-homogeneous seminorm $\tilde q \ge q$ (with $0 < p, r \le 1$) such that the canonical map between the associated local quasi-Banach spaces is nuclear in the appropriate $p$-normed sense.

Question: Does there exist a nuclear F-space that is locally pseudo-convex but not locally convex?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was resolved in the negative shortly after being posed: J.-P. Ligaud proved that every nuclear locally pseudo-convex space is locally convex, so no such F-space exists.

status_evidence.snippet: After the Conference J.P. Ligaud has shown that each nuclear locally pseudo-convex space is locally convex.
status_evidence.claim: The question was answered negatively: a nuclear locally pseudo-convex F-space is necessarily locally convex.
